transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-16
Time: 11:00 AM EDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Karen Lopez (CTO, Midtown), Luis Moreno (Head of Compliance), Tina Park (Dir Ops)

Summary (auto): quick discovery to understand Midtown's data residency, logging, and compliance constraints and evaluate Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment options. Action items captured.

Transcript:
00:00 Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alex, I'm the AE on this account, with Samir our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
00:05 Karen (CTO): Good, thanks. We wanted to cover a few very specific things around data residency and what kind of logs you keep, retention windows, that sort of thing.
00:12 Samir (Redwood SE): Great, that's what we expected. Quick agenda - we'll ask about your current stack, compliance requirements (GDPR, financial regs), logging and audit needs, then map Hosted/Dedicated/Private options to those needs.
00:20 Tina (Dir Ops): Sounds good. We have 2 main use cases: customer-facing chat summarization and internal analyst assistants. The external stuff definitely needs data to stay in EU for a subset of customers.
00:30 Luis (Compliance): And from a compliance perspective, we need auditable trails, tamper-evident logs, and contractual guarantees about data residency and subprocessors. We're SOC2 but also have region-specific requirements.
00:40 Alex: Understood. Can you tell us your current infra for model hosting? Are you running anything in-house today?
00:46 Karen: We host some models on-prem for very sensitive workflows, otherwise AWS eu-west-1. We use KMS for keys and have HSM for some signing. We're evaluating whether Redwood Hosted could be used for less sensitive flows, or whether we need Dedicated or Private.
00:58 Samir: Hoping to clarify differences - Hosted is our multi-tenant cloud offering that can run in different regions, Dedicated is reserved capacity isolated for you (still managed by Redwood), and Private is customer-managed control plane / VPC or on-prem package. For EU data residency we can pin regions.
01:12 Luis: Can you confirm whether Hosted stores request/response payloads in a way that Redwood or subprocessors could access them? We need to know retention windows and deletion semantics.
01:20 Alex: Short answer - Hosted stores telemetry and logs by default for service health; customer data retention varies by plan. For enterprise customers we have options to disable request logging and can set retention windows. We also have DPA terms and can restrict subprocessors or provide a list.
01:32 Tina: When you say "disable logging" - does that impact observability? We need kubernetes-level traces for debugging production issues.
01:38 Samir: Good point. We have telemetry tiers. You can disable full request payload logging while still sending aggregated metrics and sampling traces for debugging. For Dedicated we can do more granular controls - e.g., keep logs in your VPC and ship to your SIEM, or we can forward only hashed identifiers.
01:52 Karen: For the EU customers we need data residency at rest and in backups. Also some regulators require that logs with PII are never stored outside region.
01:58 Luis: Also encryption key control: can we manage keys in our KMS or HSM?
02:03 Samir: Yes. For Dedicated and Private deployments we support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own KMS). For Hosted we offer KMS integrations in certain plans - but if you need HSM-backed keys with full control, Private is the best fit.
02:15 Alex: Also note we can provide a contract addendum that limits data processing to the EU for specific endpoints, and our subprocessors list is part of the DPA.
02:25 Karen: What's your position on HIPAA? Not our primary concern but we have a small set of customers with healthcare data.
02:30 Luis: We do have some healthcare-related docs but the main bar for us is financial regs and GDPR.
02:35 Samir: We can support HIPAA-relevant controls; we have customers who put the service behind Dedicated or Private and sign a BAA.
02:44 Tina: Auditing - we need tamper-evident logs and retention audit to support investigations. Can you ship logs to our Splunk instance?
02:51 Samir: Yep. For Dedicated and Private we can forward logs directly to your SIEM over secure channels. Hosted can forward but depending on plan we may need to sample or redact payloads.
03:02 Karen: Regarding PII redaction: do you offer built-in redaction or tokenization?
03:07 Alex: We have pre-processing hooks and can integrate tokenization/redaction at the API gateway or client side. We also have prefix-caching so be careful with cache policies - we can configure to avoid caching PII.
03:18 Luis: And about audit logs - do you keep model input/outputs by default? If yes, for how long, and can we request deletion?
03:27 Samir: Default is 30 days for Hosted telemetry, but for enterprise customers it's configurable. We support on-demand deletion requests and programmatic deletion via the console+API. For regulated customers we often recommend Dedicated with logs shipped to customer-owned sinks.
03:41 Tina: Ok. Do you support SSO/SCIM, RBAC for different roles? We need strict separation between dev and prod and least privilege.
03:49 Alex: Yes SAML SSO, SCIM for provisioning, and role-based access controls in the Console. For Private you get full control over auth.
03:56 Karen: Network-level controls - VPC peering, private endpoints, can you do no-public-internet egress?
04:02 Samir: Yes for Dedicated and Private we use private networking. We can do VPC peering and customer-managed NAT. For Hosted we offer private endpoints in supported regions.
04:10 Luis: Any third-party subprocessors in EU? We need names and what they process.
04:14 Alex: We'll send the subprocessors list - commonly cloud infra, observability providers. We can do a DPA that limits subprocessor use and provide notices.
04:22 Karen: Performance question - our internal infra team worries that Dedicated/Private will add latency vs Hosted. Is there data?
04:29 Samir: Latency depends on proximity and instance type. Dedicated in-region capacity typically matches Hosted throughput; Private on-prem will vary based on your hardware. We can run a 24-48h benchmark with a traffic pattern you share - Samir: I'll own that.
04:40 Tina: Cost tradeoffs - short overview?
04:43 Alex: Hosted gives lowest ops overhead and pay-as-you-go; Dedicated is committed capacity - more predictable unit cost and isolation; Private is highest ops overhead but max control. We'll include a sizing/pricing spreadsheet.
04:54 Luis: Are there contractual SLAs around data residency and incident notification? We need 72-hour breach notification and tailored SLA for region-specific outages.
05:01 Alex: Standard is 72-hour notification; we can include specific clauses in enterprise agreements.
05:06 Karen: Great. I want to recap and next steps.
05:10 Alex: Recap: 1) You need EU-only residency for certain endpoints and backups; 2) You need off-host key control for the most sensitive flows; 3) Auditable, tamper-evident logs shipped to your Splunk; 4) Option to disable request payload logging in Hosted or use Dedicated/Private for stricter control.
05:27 Luis: Correct. Timeline - we're aiming to decide by end of month; pilot asap for a low-risk workflow.
05:33 Alex: Next steps: we'll send SOC2 + security whitepaper and DPA, pricing + Dedicated sizing spreadsheet; Samir will do a technical deep dive for Private/Dedicated with your infra team and run an initial benchmark.
05:45 Tina: We'll compile our regulatory Qs and send to Luis to consolidate.
05:50 Karen: Ok thanks everyone.
05:52 Alex: Thanks all - speak next week.

Notes: occasional transcription errors present ("KV cash" instead of KV cache in one snippet), some speaker labels auto-populated. Links referenced: /redwood/security-whitepaper.pdf (sent), /redwood/dpa-subprocessors.csv (to be sent).
